name: Grape Purple
lede: Grape Purple is a very deep reddish purple named for the fruit's skin, one of several grape-based names in our library that do not quite agree on a single shade.

sections.title: A fruit, several shades
sections.body:
Our library already carries a plain entry for [[grape|Grape]], at a lighter, more muted hex than this one, with Maerz and Paul dating the name to 1930, plate 47 J 12 [1]. Grape Purple is a separate, more saturated entry from the 2010 xkcd color survey, and the two names describe different points in the same small patch of purple [2]. ISCC-NBS 1955 would file Grape Purple as a very deep reddish purple [2].

The nearest standard relative is [[byzantium|Byzantium]], and the plain [[grape|Grape]] entry is itself within about 3 units of Byzantium, so all three names sit close together [1][2]. Grape skins actually carry anthocyanin pigments that shift with ripeness and variety, from pale green to near-black, so no single purple speaks for every grape [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact deep purple covers five percent or more of the canvas [4]. That is expected: it is a saturated, dark modern survey color, well outside the range aged varnish and historical pigments tend to produce [4]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [4].
